name: FlippazOne ownerWithdrawAllTo lacks onlyOwner
summary: FlippazOne, a one-NFT English auction that holds bidders' ETH, declares ownerWithdrawAllTo(address) public without onlyOwner, so anyone can send the contract's whole balance to any address. The anchor is a generalized front-running bot (contract 0xb314fd4a, EOA 0x0000000a5aab) copying 0x56d8b635's ownerWithdrawAllTo call from the mempool and placing it first in block 15084458, taking the 1.15 ETH of the only bid; a day later 0xd6efc21d called it directly and took the 4 ETH winning bid.
notes: Anchor: the bot's transaction is index 0 of block 15084458 and the copied call from 0x56d8b635 (0x8bded20c, index 25, in refs) succeeded with an empty balance; neither address is the deployer 0x7f377ee9. Like 0x1adfd037 and 0xc02bb286, it moved no ETH and is not in the campaign. campaign.mjs with --traces over the contract's whole history finds no other value-moving call; the contract's txlist has ten transactions, the last at block 15090541.

Loss is the contract's ETH outflow in the two drains: 1.15 ETH bid by 0x194a39f4 (which had funded the deployer with 0.5 ETH, so it may be the team's own seed bid) and the 4 ETH winning bid of 0x61baa493, who still received the NFT at endAuction, so the 4 ETH is the seller's lost proceeds.
